description: ecoinvent's prepared correspondence tables are retired (#141, plans/retire-prepared-correspondence.md): every ecoinvent row is now decided by this project's own matching, the element/ion rule (§3a), and the curated rows in ecoinvent-match-overrides.json. These claims pin the retirement's load-bearing outcomes: the #130 twins resolve onto the substances their own registration names; the element/ion rule's landings hold in every compartment; the origin-qualifier wall held where ecoinvent marks the qualifier by uuid alone; the joins the table used to carry (heat, the buckets, the size fractions) survive as this project's stated rows; and the ore conversion this project already ruled on still converts. Measured on the retirement build of 2026-08-23. The factor movements are the flows' movements: no factor changed its value on a flow that stayed put, but flows that moved took and surfaced factors -- factors_published shifts by a few dozen in six hundred and seventy thousand, and the proposed-factor queue grows from 132 to 204 because flows the tables had hidden behind wrong matches now ask their own factor questions.

expectations.title: ecoinvent's metaldehyde lands on the metaldehyde the JRC characterised
expectations.comment: The #130 twin: with the table retired the rows follow their own registration, 108-62-3, to the entry carrying the JRC's factors, instead of EF's uncharacterised duplicate (9002-91-9). The substance is the claim: one row lands on a factorless duplicate *flow* of the right substance, and joining the twin objects flow-by-flow is #130's work, not the retirement's.

expectations.title: ecoinvent's fenpropimorph is one substance in 3.8 and 3.12 alike
expectations.comment: The #130 twin plus a stale 3.8 registration: 3.12 registers the racemate 67564-91-4 and 3.8 registered the skeleton, so without the manual fix the retirement would split one fungicide by release.

expectations.title: Nickel II is nickel(2+) in air and soil, not only in water
expectations.comment: Plan §3a clause 2: the name decides, charge-normalised, in every compartment alike. The table used to send the air and soil rows to the element.

expectations.title: 3.8's bare zinc rows follow the newest release's identity to zinc(2+)
expectations.comment: §3a clause 1: 3.8 ships these uuids as elemental `Zinc` (7440-66-6) and 3.12 renumbers them 23713-49-7; the canonical-identities file substitutes the newest identity before matching, so the recorded name here is already the canonical one.

expectations.title: Copper ion lands on a generic copper-ion substance, not on the element and not on a guessed charge
expectations.comment: §3a clause 4: 3.12 deleted the number deliberately, and picking Cu(2+) for it would be the reinterpretation the rule refuses. The object is minted, on the `Arsenic, Ion` precedent.

expectations.title: ecoinvent's land-use-change methane stays on the land-use-change substance
expectations.comment: ecoinvent marks the qualifier by uuid alone -- the row is named plain `Methane` with the unqualified gas's number -- so the join lives in ecoinvent-match-overrides.json now that the table is gone. If this row is UNRESOLVED the uuid has changed and the override family needs re-deriving.

expectations.title: ecoinvent's waste heat is EF's waste heat, not a second heat
expectations.comment: Heat has no registry number, so the name join the table used to carry is stated in ecoinvent-match-overrides.json; without it the retirement shadow build minted a duplicate substance for all 27 rows.

expectations.title: Every TiO2-in-ore spelling converts to elemental titanium at the stated factor
expectations.comment: The 0.599 kg/kg conversion this file has carried since #260 -- plus the fourth sibling spelling, which the shadow build showed landing unconverted on titanium dioxide while its three siblings converted.

expectations.title: The five minted generic-ion substances share one spelling
expectations.comment: The follow-up named on #141 as minted-ion label harmonisation. The creation path took whichever vendor spelling arrived first, so five substances of one shape (Antimony, Arsenic, Copper, Iron, Tin) published as `X Ion` while the module that matches them spells `X, Ion` and `Thiocyanate, Ion` already publishes that shape. Renamed through `flow-object-overrides.json` names entries -- the #335 mechanism -- with the old spellings kept as alternative labels. Antimony carries the claim for the family (one selector, one substance); the other four moved in the same change and their own expectations (0396's two, 0617's, 0627's, and the #131 claim in this file) pin them under the new spelling. flow_count 14 says renamed, not replaced: the same substance, every flow following it per #7. Fails before the rename lands, which is the fail-first this project's discipline wants. Fifteen since #198: AGRIBALYSE's eleven `Antimony, ion` rows, the element's number taken off them, reach this substance by name, and one of them is in a river, a compartment none of the fourteen had. Still renamed, not replaced: the same substance, one flow more.
